facts.claim: Elounda Beach Hotel & Villas (Elounda, Crete) publishes an 'Indicative Wedding Package' that includes a dedicated consultant, legal and licence paperwork requirements, and a civil or religious ceremony outside the hotel's church or at another place of the couple's choice (the 'any other place' option is marked for civil weddings). Re-checked live; restates greece-wedding-venues fact_101 and crete-wedding-venues fact_02.

Elounda Beach's indicative package also lists: bridal bouquet, groom's boutonniere and decoration of the club car; sparkling wine and Greek wedding sweets for the couple after the ceremony; taped music during the ceremony; a wedding cake; a complimentary room for the groom's preparation from 14.00 until the ceremony; a room upgrade on the day and for the rest of the stay (subject to availability); bridal turn-down; a wedding gift; a massage for the couple the day before; breakfast in bed the next morning; and an escorted transfer to the relevant authorities to register the wedding.

Elounda Beach lists as 'Additional Available Services' (outside the indicative package): bridal gown and tuxedo rental locally, bride's hair and make-up, nail care or treatments at the Elounda Beach Spa, decoration of the wedding location with flowers, traditional Cretan lyre music during the ceremony, video and photography, cocktails, reception and children's menus, entertainment, a firework show, children's entertainers and guest thank-you gift ideas. The page publishes no minimum guest, room or night condition.
facts.conflicts: crete-wedding-venues fact_04 and greece-wedding-venues fact_103 grouped lyre music, fireworks and bridal treatments as 'wedding services'; the live page lists them under 'Additional Available Services', i.e. outside the indicative package. Limo transfer for guests and bridal treatment and hairdresser facilities appear under the separate 'Exquisite Services' list.

facts.claim: Nana Princess (Chersonissos, Crete) offers civil weddings on its private sandy beach, Greek Orthodox weddings in the private Chapel of St. George in the hotel grounds, symbolic weddings officiated by its event coordinator, and vow renewals. For symbolic weddings it offers decoration schemes including fresh flowers and exclusive use of the chosen room or venue, a flower-decorated club car for the bride, and rose petals and rice for guests. Re-checked live; restates fact_609/610 and fact_100/101.

Nana Princess publishes three named packages plus bespoke: Deluxe Dream (welcome drinks, champagne and strawberries in the honeymoon suite, an event coordinator present throughout the stay), Ultimate Passion (pre-wedding tasting dinner from the wedding menu, a massage the day before, the bride's escort to the venue in a flower-decorated club car) and Essential Elegance (private brunch at Eternal Blue for the couple and guests, an hour in the Royal Wellness Club private suite, a farewell dinner). The page shows highlights only and links each package via an 'Explore' button; full inclusions and conditions are not on the page.

Nana Princess says a dedicated event coordinator guides couples through local registry office requirements and other formalities after the date is booked; it names an external wedding planner it works with for photography, decor and flowers, and lists limousine transfers, welcome gifts, honeymoon packages and room upgrades (subject to availability). Its vow-renewal ceremony states that beverages are not included in the accompanying dinner.

Abaton Island Resort & Spa's weddings page (checked live) offers set wedding packages or a custom wedding at the couple's chosen venue, with customisable elements listed as ceremony, music and entertainment, flowers, additional decor, beauty services, cocktail bar, gala dinner, additional services and planning, photography and video. The page still links only the 2025-2026 wedding brochure; no 2026-2027 brochure is linked.

Elounda Collection (Elounda SA Hotels & Resorts: Elounda Peninsula, Porto Elounda, Elounda Mare) publishes a wedding packages PDF, linked from eloundapeninsula.com, with separate Civil, Orthodox and Symbolic packages plus a wedding services section (ceremony locations, venues, reception, dinner menus, beverages, entertainment, boat transfer, additional services). Re-checked live; restates crete-wedding-venues fact_15.

Elounda Collection's civil and Orthodox packages (both titled 'Lavish Wedding Package') include: reservation of date and time; choice of ceremony venue; documentation assistance and settlement of the wedding licence with the couple and the local Municipality Office; two witnesses if needed; ceremony set-up with a table and seasonal flower display; bouquet and boutonniere; rose petals; a separate room for the groom to change; pre-recorded music during the ceremony; drinks in the bride's and groom's rooms during preparation; transfer of the couple within the hotel's premises to the ceremony; a short fireworks display; room decoration after the ceremony; a menu tasting for two (beverages excluded); champagne breakfast in bed; and a round-trip transfer to the Registry Office with the hotel's executive. Room upgrade, early check-in and late check-out are subject to availability. Restates crete fact_16.

Elounda Collection's package conditions and exclusions: each package 'is valid provided that the couple will be staying for a minimum of three nights in one of our hotels'; the civil package rate 'does not include the Municipal fees' and the Orthodox package rate 'does not include the Metropolis fee' (amounts stripped; a fee applies, subject to change). Documents must be Apostille-certified one by one, translated into Greek, emailed for approval at least 4 weeks before and couriered to the hotel at the couple's own cost at least 3 weeks before; all documents must be issued within 3 months of the wedding date. Restates crete fact_17.

Exact wording in the Elounda Collection PDF (civil documentation page): "The marriage has to be registered by the couple at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days after the ceremony. If the wedding takes place on a Friday (or weekends), the registration of the wedding takes place the following Monday." The Orthodox documentation page repeats it with "(or weekend) the registration" (singular, no comma).

Elounda Collection's Orthodox package documents list adds church-specific requirements: certificates of marital status, a Certificate of No Impediment from the church parish, baptism certificates (one partner must be Christian Orthodox and both must be baptised Orthodox, Roman Catholic or Protestant), and an announcement of the wedding in the local newspaper at least 8 days before. Approval is by the Metropolis. (Venue-published requirement; legal meaning to be confirmed against government or embassy sources by batch B.)

Elounda Collection's symbolic ceremony / renewal of vows package includes date and time reservation, bouquet and boutonniere, two witnesses if needed and the hotel's official representative at the ceremony, sparkling wine and a single-tier wedding cake for the couple, room decoration, spa facility use and breakfast in bed. The PDF states: "Symbolic weddings /renewal of vows are not legally recognized from the Greek constitution." The same three-night minimum stay applies.

Grace Hotel (Auberge Collection, Imerovigli, Santorini) prices weddings as a flat venue fee rather than a package. For celebrations over 50 people the fee includes exclusive use of the selected event spaces, tables and chairs, lounge furniture and bars, glassware, china, silverware and napkins, set-up and breakdown, event staffing, screens and room dividers, and transport between the hotel and the event site for guests staying at Grace Hotel. For 50 guests or fewer it includes exclusive use of the selected spaces, tables and chairs, tableware, a wedding arbour, set-up and breakdown, and transport to and from the event site. Re-checked live; restates greece-wedding-venues fact_03.

Grace Hotel provides a dedicated event manager for venue details but requires a wedding planner for all weddings, involved at least 3 months before the date. Menus: for up to 30 guests, offering a choice of three pre-selected mains is 'for a charge' with a minimum four-course menu. Guests may book individually; a room block or resort buyout is priced by the Sales Manager on request, and no minimum number of rooms must be booked. A DJ or live band is permitted (the hotel offers recommendations), and a private lounge for the wedding party is available from 8am. Restates fact_03/fact_04.

Euphoria Resort (Kolymvari, Chania, Crete) offers three wedding options (Elxi, Pathos, Eros) for 'an informal wedding or renewal of vows'; each includes a choice of hotel venues (beaches and poolside), venue decoration (lanterns, petals, covered chairs, floral table display), bouquet and buttonhole, two witnesses and the hotel's official representative, 'a certificate of informal marriage from the hotel', petals and rice, sparkling wine and a wedding cake after the ceremony (for up to 10, 20 or 30 guests by option), ceremony music (pre-recorded, or a jazz musician in Eros), photographs from the hotel photographer and a gift. Pathos and Eros add spa treatments, dinners and 'your own event coordinator'. Re-checked live; restates crete fact_400/401.

Euphoria Resort states its options 'are complete packages, and their items are not interchangeable. If you decide not to use one of the services, no refund or alternative can be given'; packages may be amended at extra cost ('with respective cost'), and offers are subject to availability. Buffet, seated and cocktail receptions, beverage packages, open bar, custom cakes and entertainment are listed as other services priced on request. A honeymoon package is offered free to couples who book a wedding package and stay at the hotel.

Santa Marina, a Luxury Collection Resort (Ornos, Mykonos), says on its live Weddings & Celebrations page that it has sea-view venues and a traditional whitewashed stone chapel, and an experienced team of wedding planners covering bespoke menus, floral arrangements and elopement parties. The page links a weddings brochure and an event menu but publishes no package inclusions, conditions or ceremony types in its text. Restates greece-wedding-venues fact_10.

Canaves Collection (Oia, Santorini) describes a tailored approach using its venues, wedding planners and hand-picked vendors, with ceremony venues for up to 30 (Panorama Balcony, Canaves Oia Suites), 40 (Veranda, Canaves Sunday) and 25 guests (Sunset Terrace, Canaves Epitome). It links 'Wedding Package Options' but the page text lists no package inclusions. Re-checked live; restates greece-wedding-venues fact_06/07.

Canaves Collection's wedding request form lists ceremony types Religious, Civil, Symbolic and Vow Renewal, and selectable extras including flower arch, gazebo, bridesmaid's bouquet, wedding crowns, bombonieres, guest welcome gifts, photographer, videographer, bridal bouquet, wedding cake, fireworks, 'Preparation of Wedding Documents', DJ, live bands, traditional musicians accompanying the bride, harpist and lighting. These are enquiry-form options, not confirmed package inclusions.

Katikies Hotels (Santorini and Mykonos) say their events and concierge team plans and manages every wedding detail; 'Micro weddings' are listed under 'Packages ideas' as small, exclusive ceremonies, with no inclusions published. The enquiry form lists 'Hotel Take over' as an event type. Venues marked ideal for wedding ceremonies include Botrini's Restaurant at Katikies Santorini (60 seated) and the Upper deck at Katikies Mykonos (50 seated). Re-checked live; restates greece-wedding-venues fact_300/301/302.

Amirandes, Grecotel (Gouves, near Heraklion, Crete) says couples can exchange vows at its VIP Beach or chapel, choose from its dining venues, and plan with dedicated wedding specialists, for celebrations up to 300 guests; meal plans offered for groups are breakfast, half board or all-inclusive. No wedding package inclusions are published on the page. Re-checked live; restates crete fact_104/105.
facts.conflicts: The events page facility list says 'Just 15 mins from Heraklion International Airport'; crete-wedding-venues fact_106 cites 18 km from the resort page. Time and distance are not in conflict but the article should cite one.

facts.claim: Abaton's 2025-2026 wedding brochure (re-read live; file last modified September 2025) lists under 'The Basics' ceremony, coordination services, photography, videography, Chiavari chairs, chair covers and table set-up decoration, and says 'Your Wedding Coordinator will prepare every last detail'. Flowers (bridal party flowers, wedding arch, site floral decor), music (piano, saxophone, guitar, violin, DJ) and beauty services are separate sections, and hair, make-up, nails, spa, buttonholes, a wedding cake ('for a minimum of 30 people'), DJ, fireworks, centrepieces, rose petals, photography and video are listed as additional services with indicative costs (amounts stripped). Each named venue carries its own venue fee (a fee applies; amounts stripped).

Abaton's brochure Terms & Conditions state: 'All packages are subject to availability and do not include accommodation'; 'All packages are valid with a minimum accommodation booking of 10 rooms for minimum 2 nights (depending on guests number)'; 'All packages are valid with a minimum of 20 guests wedding reception booking (maximum capacity 300 guests)'; and 'All packages are complete and package items are not interchangeable.' Gala dinner buffets state a minimum of 60 guests. Re-checked live; restates crete fact_113.

Myconian Collection (Elia, Mykonos) says it can 'prepare the stage for your own team or provide a complete event solution', listing invitations, travel logistics, VIP transportation, menus, specialist cakes, wines, flowers, favours, lighting, sound and music, honeymoon planning and fireworks over the bay. It says it assists in officiating ceremonies across all denominations and has certified halal and kosher kitchens. No package tiers, inclusions or conditions are published. Re-checked live; restates greece-wedding-venues fact_12/14.

Canaves Collection's Exclusives & Buyouts page (updated November 2026) offers full-property buyouts per hotel: Canaves Epitome 53 rooms and up to 170 guests, Canaves Oia Suites 48 rooms and 120 guests, Canaves Ena 18 rooms and 45 guests, Canaves Sunday 10 rooms and 22 guests, with a 'Request Your Buyout Proposal' form; no buyout inclusions or conditions are published. Re-checked live; restates greece-wedding-venues fact_08.

Nana Princess, Euphoria Resort and Elounda Beach say room upgrades for the couple are subject to availability; Elounda Collection also makes early check-in and late check-out subject to availability. None of these venues guarantees an upgrade in its published package wording.

Mystique, a Luxury Collection Hotel (Oia, Santorini) says its wedding specialists take care of every aspect and help organise the wedding, its venues serve as the ceremony backdrop and the team will find the setting; it offers Elios Spa treatments and getting ready with the bridal party in a suite. No package inclusions, conditions or ceremony types are published. Re-checked live; restates greece-wedding-venues fact_303.

Melenos Art Boutique Hotel (in the village of Lindos, Rhodes, next to the Lindos acropolis) says its wedding coordinators can arrange a civil ceremony, a symbolic ceremony or a traditional Orthodox wedding. Once a couple chooses the hotel they receive a detailed schedule of the coming months and a costing sheet setting out the deadlines; the coordinator organises tasks, outlines a budget, builds an itinerary of events, assists throughout planning, meets the couple on arrival and stays with them until the ceremony. Re-check of Greece pack fact_104 and fact_105.

Melenos says its wedding planner takes care of the required legal documentation, including filing documents, marriage licence registration and the government and administrative fees, and official witnesses can be provided on request. (The page says fees exist and that the coordinator attends to them; it does not say whether they sit inside or outside the costing.) Re-check of Greece pack fact_105.

Melenos suggests reserving the entire hotel for a minimum of three nights for a wedding (a suggestion, not stated as a condition); additional guests can stay at the Melenos Apartments and Studios in the village, a 10 minute walk from the hotel. Re-check of Greece pack fact_106.

Melenos coordinators assist with decor (seasonal flowers from the hotel garden or a special order from a local florist; bouquets, corsages, centrepieces; the hotel's own decorative objects), details for Orthodox ceremonies such as Jordan almonds on a silver tray, and the reception menu (traditional Greek with South Mediterranean influences, modified for dietary needs). It lists other services the coordinators can organise as additional services: rehearsal dinner on the Melenos terrace, pre-wedding welcome cocktail party, professional photographer and videographer, hair and make-up artists, private boat excursion, live music, donkeys to carry the couple to the ceremony and a candlelit dinner for the couple after the ceremony. Re-check of Greece pack fact_107.

Angsana Corfu Resort & Spa (Corfu) links a 2026 wedding brochure from its Weddings & Honeymoons page, alongside a real weddings page, a wedding venues page and a wedding proposal request form. Re-check of Greece pack fact_305.

Angsana Corfu's 2026 wedding brochure lists its ceremony venues under the heading 'Symbolic Wedding Ceremony Venues': Vertigo Sky Bar (outdoor, maximum 250, available mid-May to the end of September, weather permitting) and Oribu Garden (outdoor, maximum 30, April to October, weather permitting). Reception venues are Vertigo Sky Bar (outdoor, maximum 250, end of May to end of September, weather permitting), Oribu Restaurant (outdoor and indoor, maximum 150, April, May, September and October) and Oribu Garden (outdoor, maximum 30, April to October). The brochure does not mention civil or Orthodox ceremonies or a package inclusion list.
facts.conflicts: Brochure gives Vertigo Sky Bar availability as 'mid-May' for ceremonies but 'the end of May' for receptions.

facts.claim: Angsana Corfu's 2026 brochure describes a 'Special Wedding Offer': a credit towards a next stay at any Banyan Tree or Angsana hotel, and, for wedding bookings above a stated minimum food and beverage spend, one complimentary night for the couple in a One-Bedroom Sea View Suite or Ionian Sea View Villa with private pool, a welcome amenity (champagne, fruit and traditional sweets) and in-room breakfast the day after the wedding. The amounts are omitted here; the offer is conditional on a minimum food and beverage spend.

Grand Resort Lagonissi (Athens Riviera) says couples can take advantage of the resort's 'exclusive wedding and honeymoon packages', with a stay in a sea view suite, beachfront bungalow or waterfront private villa. The Weddings & Ceremonies page names five venues (Uranus open-air terrace for a 'Grand Wedding Gala', Veghera on the south water edge of the peninsula, La Piscina garden and pool, Aphrodite, Villa Elounda garden near a private sandy beach) but publishes no package inclusion list, conditions or ceremony types. Re-check of Greece pack fact_208.

Grand Resort Lagonissi lists its wedding services as: wedding assistance from its Events team; chefs and pastry chefs for wedding cakes and desserts; private party planning in a suite or by the beachfront; professional designers for flowers and table and venue decoration; DJs with sound and lighting technical support; specialised services such as photography, special effects and limousine rentals; a 'Honeymoon Suite'; bridal treatments and beauty facilities; and dinners by a private pool with a personal chef. It does not say which of these sit inside a package.

Costa Navarino (Messinia, south-west Peloponnese) says traditional religious marriages can be held at the chapel of St Samson within Navarino Dunes or at St Eleni at Navarino Agora, and civil ceremonies can be arranged on request indoors in town halls or outdoors (beach, boat, hilltop, beside a stream). Its weddings page names The Romanos, a Luxury Collection Resort, W Costa Navarino and Mandarin Oriental, Costa Navarino (eight indoor and outdoor spaces from 62 sqm to 868 sqm) and refers to four 5-star resorts; enquiries go through a weddings email and booking calendars. It publishes no wedding package or inclusion list. Re-check of Greece pack fact_209 and fact_210.

Grecotel Corfu Imperial (Kommeno, Corfu) offers weddings and vow renewals with dedicated wedding specialists, customised menus and 'trusted vendors'. Named venues are Yali Waterfront Restaurant on a deck above the water, Aristos Restaurant for up to 50 guests and the private island 'Nissaki' for up to 50 guests; enquiries go through a request for proposal form. The page publishes no package inclusion list, conditions or ceremony types. Re-check of Greece pack fact_108.

Atrium Prestige (south Rhodes) names ceremony and reception venues (Amphitheater a few steps from the beach, described as ideal for larger events; the private Tsambika chapel reached across a bridge, offered 'for a more traditional wedding ceremony'; Lachania private beach; Golden Dome; Panoramic Terrace; Thallassa restaurant for receptions; Kalithea main bar for the party, with fireworks). For couples seeking a civil ceremony, its wedding specialist assists with all arrangements needed to obtain the marriage licence. It also offers symbolic ceremonies, elopements and vow renewals. Re-check of Greece pack fact_307.

Atrium Prestige lists wedding services on its weddings page: bridal suite (a sea view villa with personal pool to get ready in), decoration and flowers, bridal make-up and hairstyling, on-site photographer, bridal bouquet, wedding cake, wedding reception with a menu tasting with the chef, DJ or live music (violin, guitar or bouzouki), fireworks, spa treatments, honeymoon villa, private dinner for two, couple's massage (a complimentary hydrobath for stays of 5 nights and above), a complimentary in-room offer of fruit or sweets with sparkling wine, and a romantic boat trip. It does not group these into a named package or say which carry a charge.

As at November 2026, the Australian Embassy in Athens lists among its notarial services witnessing application forms for, and issuing, Certificates of No Impediment (CNI) and witnessing notices of intended marriage, plus legalisation of signatures and seals by authentication or apostille. An appointment is required for all notarial services (Monday to Friday, 9:00am to 12:30pm), although CNI and apostille documents can be submitted by post; CNIs and apostilled documents are available for collection within two working days unless same-day collection has been arranged. The Embassy does not provide legal advice, honorary consuls cannot provide notarial services, notarial service fees apply and an additional fee applies for return by post. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. Re-check of Greece pack fact_212 and Crete pack fact_207.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Getting married overseas' page (last updated 18/08/2026, re-read live 2026-11-11) gives general advice only and says some countries ask you to prove you are not already married, with each country deciding what proof it accepts; the most common documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages. The destination may have further rules, and Smartraveller says it cannot tell you what you will need. DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need one, whether you can get it in Australia and whether it needs an authentication or apostille. Local authorities may also ask for divorce papers, a deceased spouse's death certificate, and an original birth certificate and passport. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. Re-check of Greece pack fact_206 and Crete pack fact_208.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller says you cannot register an overseas marriage in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid under the law of the country where it happened and would have been valid under Australian law had it occurred in Australia; a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of marriage but may not be usable as proof of a name change (check with your local registry); talk to a lawyer to confirm validity. The Wedded Advisor confirms current requirements. Re-check of Greece pack fact_207 and Crete pack fact_209.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's overall advice level for Greece is 'Exercise normal safety precautions' (page updated 30 September 2026, still current at 11 November 2026, re-read live 2026-11-11). It says wildfires occur during the extended summer period from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, prompting evacuations; heatwaves are frequent over the summer months; and Greece is in an active seismic zone. Re-check of Crete pack fact_204 and fact_205.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece page says Australians entering the Schengen area for a short stay (90 days or less) on an Australian passport register biometric details such as fingerprints and a photo on arrival under the EES, need take no action beforehand, pay nothing for EES registration, and may face delays at border crossings; during peak season severe traffic congestion occurs in the main cities and on the islands; and only licensed taxis should be used, with the meter running. Re-check of Crete pack fact_206.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's Greece page says to get comprehensive travel insurance before you leave and closely read the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS); it must cover all medical costs overseas, including evacuation, which the Australian Government will not pay; if you can't afford travel insurance you shouldn't travel. There is no agreement between Australia and Greece for free healthcare, so tourists pay for all medical care, including hospital stays and evacuation, and payment is required before leaving the facility. Check the policy covers the whole trip including stopovers, and know the exclusions (some activities, such as going on a cruise, may cost extra to cover).

As at November 2026, Smartraveller's 'Travel insurance' page (current URL https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/travel-essentials/travel-insurance, last updated 18/08/2026; the old /before-you-go/insurance/travel-insurance URL returns 404) says to always read the PDS before buying (inclusions, exclusions, definitions, claims process, emergency support); choose a policy covering every country including stopovers and transit points; check whether the policy covers cancellations if the advice level goes up after you have booked; insurers exclude many activities from standard policies, even common ones like going on a cruise, so you may need to pay extra; you must declare all pre-existing conditions, and declare everything upfront or you may void the policy; credit card insurance often covers fewer situations and usually has to be activated; basic (medical-only) policies usually don't cover cancellation costs; travel insurance can cover cancellation costs if plans change, so find out what your policy covers before you buy.

Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens (Vouliagmeni, Athens Riviera) headlines its weddings page 'Luxury Greece Wedding Packages in Athens' and says it provides complete event coordination for ceremonies and receptions; couples reserve exclusive waterfront venues across its 30-hectare (75-acre) estate for 10 to 1,000 guests; its event specialists manage banquet menus, seating and guest room blocks; options range from a single-day ceremony to a three-day destination itinerary with spa treatments and private beach access; it has an in-house wedding planner and offers vow renewals. Re-check of Greece pack fact_200 and fact_201.

Amanzoe (Kranidi, east Peloponnese) says on its celebrations page that it hosts weddings of all sizes with personalised experiences and invites couples to contact it for a full proposal ('from conception through to execution'). It publishes no wedding package, inclusion list, conditions or ceremony types.

Four Seasons Astir Palace Athens publishes 'Wedding Inclusions' that couples who book a wedding receive: one night of accommodation (the wedding night) for the couple; tailor-made amenities on the wedding night; a designed menu tasting for up to four guests; planning assistance from a dedicated in-house wedding specialist; a dedicated service team on the day; choice of venues; premium tables, chairs and linens; Sambonet silver and Rosenthal fine bone china; high-speed internet throughout the stay; and access to waterfront and garden locations as photography backdrops. It does not state ceremony types or a minimum guest count.

Four Seasons Astir Palace Athens says its on-site wedding specialist works 'with you or your consultant' to reserve dates, plan the schedule, coordinate food and beverage and assist with other arrangements; the team can arrange flowers with its preferred floral designers or work with the florist of the couple's choice; it can provide a list of recommended vendors such as photographers and entertainers; local transport for the couple or guests can be arranged on request; select public spaces may be open for wedding parties subject to availability; and exclusive use of one of four restaurants (Pelagos, Helios, Taverna 37, Mercato) is offered for private dining. Special linen colours and designs are available on request.

Melenos's separate weddings site (linked from the hotel's weddings page) names two ceremony locations at the hotel, the Blue Balcony and the Magical Garden, and also offers vow renewals, commitment ceremonies, baby naming ceremonies and anniversaries. It publishes no named package or inclusion list beyond the hotel weddings page.

Grand Resort Lagonissi's Weddings & Celebrations overview refers to 'special wedding packages' and 'exclusive wedding packages', says its wedding planner can tailor any wedding to the couple, and says its venues host weddings, receptions, christenings, galas and private events for up to 1,200 guests. It links a weddings brochure PDF dated 2022 (uploads/2022/07).
facts.conflicts: Overview gives events up to 1,200 guests (all event types); no per-venue wedding capacity on the Weddings & Ceremonies page.

facts.claim: Grand Resort Lagonissi's weddings brochure (PDF uploaded July 2022, linked from the live Weddings & Celebrations page) shows an on-site chapel, St Dimitrios; lists services including a personal wedding planner, DJs with sound and lighting, photography, bridal wear, wedding suits, favours, special effects, limousine rentals, chefs, pastry chefs and floral and table designers; says the resort 'returns their trust by offering them their stay as a gift' with a honeymoon suite for the wedding night (fruit, treats, breakfast in bed, champagne); and its enquiry form asks whether the ceremony is in a church, at the hotel or elsewhere. Seated capacities include Uranus and Cosmos Ballroom 600 buffet / 700 set menu, La Piscina 450 buffet, Veghera 300 / 350 and Aphrodite 260 / 300.
facts.conflicts: Brochure dates from 2022 and still gives fax contacts and grandresort.gr addresses; the live Weddings & Ceremonies page lists a similar service set but does not repeat the complimentary wedding-night stay. Treat the brochure terms as possibly superseded.

insider_details.detail: Read the package condition lines before the inclusions: Elounda Collection packages need the couple to stay at least three nights, and Abaton's need at least 20 reception guests plus a 10-room, two-night booking, while Grace Hotel sets no room minimum at all. Put guest count, rooms and nights on the first line of any comparison.

'Complete package, items not interchangeable' is a real clause: Euphoria and Abaton both say unused items are not swapped, and Euphoria says no refund is given. If a couple will not use the cake or photographer, ask for a custom quote rather than a package.

Paperwork help is not the same as paperwork done: Elounda Collection assists with the licence, but the couple must Apostille each document separately, have them translated, email copies four weeks ahead, courier originals three weeks ahead at their own cost, and register the marriage in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days. Build the document timeline into the planning calendar for Australian couples, who will be sourcing documents from home.

Symbolic ceremony packages are the simplest to run but carry no legal weight: Elounda Collection states symbolic weddings and vow renewals are not legally recognised, and Euphoria issues an 'informal marriage' certificate. Couples wanting a legal marriage should either book a civil or Orthodox package or marry legally in Australia first.

Santorini clifftop hotels often sell space, not a package: Grace Hotel's flat venue fee covers exclusive use of the chosen spaces, furniture, staffing and guest transport but requires an outside planner, and Canaves quotes full-property buyouts by hotel. Budget planner fees separately when comparing a Santorini venue with a Crete resort package.

'Coordinator' means different things: Nana Princess's Deluxe Dream has a coordinator present throughout the stay, Euphoria includes 'your own event coordinator' only in its two upper options, Elounda Beach names a dedicated consultant, and Grace Hotel gives an event manager for venue details only. Ask who runs the day itself.

Package pages use the word loosely: Four Seasons Astir Palace lists ten named wedding inclusions, Melenos sends a costing sheet with deadlines, while Lagonissi, Costa Navarino, Corfu Imperial and Amanzoe give no inclusion list and work from a proposal. Ask every venue for its inclusions in writing before comparing.

Legal paperwork is not handled the same way everywhere: Melenos's coordinator files documents and registers the licence, Atrium Prestige assists civil couples to obtain the licence, and Angsana Corfu's 2026 brochure lists symbolic ceremony venues only. Ask which ceremony type the package is built for before signing.

Rooms can be a condition rather than an add-on: Melenos suggests taking the whole hotel for at least three nights, and Four Seasons' event specialists manage guest room blocks, so ask whether the package depends on a room commitment and for how many nights.

Seasonal venue windows shape the date: Angsana Corfu's Vertigo Sky Bar runs roughly late May to the end of September and Oribu Restaurant only in the shoulder months, and Smartraveller flags June to September wildfires and summer heatwaves, so ask for the weather back-up venue in writing.

Supplier rules differ: Four Seasons will work with the couple's own florist and its specialist works 'with you or your consultant', while others name in-house services; ask whether outside suppliers are allowed and on what terms.

Insurance is part of the package decision: Smartraveller says read the PDS, cover every stopover and check cancellation cover if the advice level rises after booking, and there is no free healthcare agreement with Greece. Line up policy cancellation terms against the venue's deposit terms.
